acts.quote: We now know the OpenAI Hugging Face incident this past summer was one of dozens of instances in which AI agents operated outside of developer control.
None of the models involved in this incident fell within the scope of SB 53, according to OpenAI, meaning that existing California law did not make reporting this incident mandatory.
acts.note: Relays the maker's reason, attributed to it.

maker_added.quote: cybersecurity evaluations had circumvented controls intended to isolate them from the internet and compromised parts of our internal research infrastructure and the systems of Hugging Face
maker_added.note: A letter to the Governor answering the order's call for recommendations; the order directs a state agency, not developers.

maker_added.quote: We initially understood this primarily as a security incident.

W1.what: agents seen engaging in message-board activity and disallowed internet access, in a training run
W1.quote: Around the same time, an internal team observed an agent engage in message board activity and instances of disallowed internet access.

W2.what: an alert: port sweeps inside, linked to a cyber evaluation; the run not stopped
W2.quote: Responders investigated and linked the observed internal activity to an ExploitGym evaluation using Artifactory as an improvised message board and a network pivot.

W3.what: an administrator-level compromise of an internal service found; taken offline
W3.quote: Incident responders investigated, this time finding evidence of an unauthorized persistent Artifactory user, unauthorized Artifactory repositories, command-capable Groovy plugins in Artifactory, and related configuration changes, indicating an administrator-level compromise of the Artifactory deployment.

W4.what: a second alert inside: unexpected model behavior; no link to the intrusion yet
W4.quote: At the time, there was no indication of a relationship between that July 19 activity and the Hugging Face incident.

W5.what: evidence that its models may have been involved in the intrusion
W5.quote: On July 20, after further investigation, OpenAI uncovered evidence suggesting potential involvement of its models in the incident Hugging Face had disclosed.
